assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction supplied the essential physical principles for reliable quantum information despite decoherence.
assessment.attribution: Shor established the transformative error-correction framework, Steane made codes operationally powerful, and Kitaev provided decisive topological fault-tolerance concepts.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have shaped all major hardware platforms and are now being tested through increasingly substantial logical-qubit demonstrations.
uncertainties: Large-scale fault-tolerant computation has not yet been achieved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong, controllable light-matter interaction on a chip into a robust experimental regime and changed quantum-device physics.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied a foundational dispersive-theory formulation, while Wallraff and Schoelkopf established its compelling experimental realization.
assessment.maturity: It is reproducible across laboratories and underlies much of present superconducting quantum science.
uncertainties: Credit also extends importantly to Steven M. Girvin and to a broad experimental lineage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks have enabled a qualitatively new precision frontier, with consequences for timekeeping, metrology and fundamental tests.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept and Ye drove major precision and performance advances.
assessment.maturity: Independent systems have repeatedly achieved extraordinary accuracy and are approaching practical redefinition-level capability.
uncertainties: The eventual institutional adoption of optical clocks as the primary time standard remains incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their theoretical architecture for trapped-ion processing and simulation made quantum information a concrete laboratory physics programme.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller form an unusually clear and tightly linked partnership between seminal proposals and the field they initiated.
assessment.maturity: The proposals have been realized and generalized across leading ion-trap experiments over decades.
uncertainties: The contribution overlaps conceptually with wider quantum-information theory and experimental ion-trap development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade turned neutral atoms into programmable, strongly interacting quantum many-body systems with remarkable control.
assessment.attribution: Lukin supplied central blockade and many-body concepts, while Browaeys and Grangier made decisive experimental advances.
assessment.maturity: Large coherent arrays and reproducible analog simulation now demonstrate the robustness of the platform.
uncertainties: The division of priority among the several foundational theory and experiment groups needs particularly careful examination.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry provided an exceptionally sensitive quantum-mechanical method for measuring inertial and gravitational quantities.
assessment.attribution: Bordé developed central interferometric concepts, and Kasevich and Pritchard drove landmark precision implementations.
assessment.maturity: Its methods are long established, widely reproduced and influential in precision measurement.
uncertainties: The appropriate boundary between atom interferometry and the broader atomic-precision-measurement tradition is not sharp.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ground-state cooling and coherent control of mechanical modes made a mesoscopic mechanical system manifestly quantum.
assessment.attribution: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg and Cleland each made central experimental and conceptual contributions to modern quantum optomechanics.
assessment.maturity: Ground-state preparation, measurement backaction and quantum control have been convincingly reproduced in diverse architectures.
uncertainties: The field has several indispensable pioneers, making a three-person attribution difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multiphoton entanglement and satellite links made quantum communication a strikingly capable physical technology over unprecedented distances.
assessment.attribution: Pan has provided unusually sustained leadership spanning multiphoton experiments, quantum repeaters and satellite demonstrations.
assessment.maturity: The experiments are technically mature and independently influential, though satellite communication remains an evolving platform.
uncertainties: The nomination combines several related achievements and may underrepresent foundational contributors to quantum communication.
